_about: Machine-readable waiver policy for the blocking dependency audit in
Every entry MUST carry: id, package, reason, mitigation, added, expires, review_owner.
scripts/ci/dep_audit_policy.py turns the active entries into pip-audit
--ignore-vuln-id flags and FAILS THE BUILD when an entry is expired or when
expires is farther out than max_waiver_days (no permanent waivers).
JSON (not YAML) on purpose: it is parsed with the Python standard library only,
so the policy gate works in every CI job without installing PyYAML.
Adding a waiver is a security decision, not a CI convenience. Prefer fixing the
dependency, replacing it, or narrowing the audit scope first.

waivers.reason: Minerva timing attack on the P-256 curve in python-ecdsa. The upstream project considers side-channel attacks out of scope and there is no planned fix, so no patched version exists to upgrade to.
waivers.mitigation: ecdsa is pulled in transitively by python-jose[cryptography]. This project signs and verifies JWTs with HS256 only and never performs ECDSA signing, key generation, or ECDH; the affected code path is unreachable. Signature verification is not affected by the advisory.

rejected_or_unnecessary.decision: NOT WAIVED — removed from the audit surface instead
rejected_or_unnecessary.reason: nltk is not a dependency of this project: it appears in no file under requirements/. It entered the audited environment only because the job ran `pip install safety pip-audit` into the project interpreter, and `safety` requires `nltk>=3.9`. The advisory (model-artifact APIs bypassing nltk.pathsec) has no patched release.
rejected_or_unnecessary.resolution: security-scan.yml now (1) installs the scanners into a throwaway .scanner-venv that is never an audit target, and (2) runs pip-audit in requirements mode (-r), so the audited surface is exactly the declared dependency graph. A waiver would have hidden a real signal forever; scoping removed the false one.
